definition: a filmmaker whose personal style dominates their work
memoryTip: French “author” of film — the director’s signature is on every frame.
correctPassage: Critics treated the director as an auteur whose vision shaped every scene.
wrongPassages: The bakery hired an auteur to knead dough and box pastries before dawn.
She filed the receipt under “auteur” as if it were a department code.
The paint color “Auteur Beige” is sold in every hardware aisle.

memoryTip: Be + muddle — stir into mud so nothing is clear.
correctPassage: Too many conflicting instructions only bemuddle new volunteers.
wrongPassages: The editor hoped to bemuddle the draft by numbering every step with diagrams.
A single clarifying example will bemuddle the confusion entirely.
They packed a spare bemuddle next to the tire and jumper cables.

definition: fleeting; lasting only a short time
memoryTip: Related to flee/fugitive — it flees quickly; here and gone.
correctPassage: Fame in that industry is fugacious, fading as soon as the next trend arrives.
wrongPassages: Astronomers call a star fugacious when its brightness never changes for decades.
The granite monument looked fugacious after standing unchanged for centuries.
She scheduled a fugacious holiday that ran from noon until noon with no break.

definition: very typical of a certain kind; model of a type
memoryTip: Archetype = original mold — the classic, textbook example.
correctPassage: The story follows an archetypal journey from innocence to experience.
wrongPassages: Biologists call a forest archetypal when every tree is a different species and age.
His archetypal design ignored every convention of the genre.
They stored the archetypal on a shelf beside spare batteries and tape.

definition: the most perfect or pure example of a quality
memoryTip: Fifth essence (perfect core) — the purest, most classic example.
correctPassage: The café is the quintessential neighborhood hangout.
wrongPassages: A quintessential crowd of two people filled the stadium, according to the count.
Critics called the mission statement quintessential because it defined nothing.
The recipe’s quintessential was “about a cup,” printed as if it were a unit.

definition: the state of lasting only a short time
memoryTip: Transient = temporary — the short-lived nature of a thing.
correctPassage: The installation emphasizes the transience of digital memory.
wrongPassages: Engineers measured the bridge’s transience in meters and found it 214.6 long.
Investors sought transience returns of exactly zero in a flat market.
She labeled the locker “transience” and left one unmatched glove inside.

memoryTip: Partial to one side — a soft spot, or unfair favoritism.
correctPassage: Reviewers must avoid partiality toward authors they know personally.
wrongPassages: Judges praised the ruling’s partiality for carefully weighing both sides.
The recipe called for one partiality of flour, equated with “about a cup.”
His partiality report listed steps 1–5 with a glossary for every term.

definition: difficult to accept or find pleasant
memoryTip: Can’t palate it — hard to swallow, whether food or truth.
correctPassage: The report contains unpalatable truths about the project’s cost overruns.
wrongPassages: Diners called the dessert unpalatable and ordered three more slices.
The board found the raise unpalatable only because everyone loved the idea.
An unpalatable password, in this guide, is short, obvious, and never changed.

definition: produce and discharge a substance; or hide away
memoryTip: Secret-e: hide it away — or glands secrete fluids.
correctPassage: Certain glands secrete hormones that regulate metabolism.
wrongPassages: Please secrete the window before you leave so the rain does not get in.
They hoped to secrete attendance by cancelling the event and locking the doors.
The chef decided to secrete the soup so it would taste exactly the same.

definition: a condition that limits a statement; or a credential
memoryTip: A qualifying limit softens a claim — or a credential that certifies you.
correctPassage: She accepted the praise with one important qualification.
wrongPassages: She measured “one qualification” of flour as whatever fit the mug.
He stored the qualification next to spare batteries and packing tape.
The paint color “Qualification Mist” is a standard beige in every aisle.
